description: The Unified Cropland Layer is a global cropland map for 2014 assembled from the best existing cropland map in each country. The figshare record says the fittest national map was chosen by a multi-criteria analysis of four criteria (legend adequacy, spatial resolution, timeliness and confidence), then the maps were resampled to 250 m on a reference grid with averaging and joined into one layer. It was published by François Waldner, with the final version (v2-3) posted on 19 March 2016 as a GeoTIFF of about 355 MB, a preview image and a paper PDF, downloadable and free under CC BY 4.0, with global coverage. Caveats: quality varies by country with the source map chosen, and the layer is not updated after 2014. For simulation it gives a consistent cropland extent to overlay with hazards such as floods and droughts, to estimate exposed farmland per region and to weight rural road and irrigation service areas. Related catalogue records include the IIASA-IFPRI percent cropland map for Africa, the Crop Map of England (CROME) and the global grassland class extent 30 m.
